Stormy Buonantony|IOWA OVER 7.5 WINS (-1.summary: Buonantony returns to a total she wrote up and cashed last year, backing Kirk Ferentz in year 28. Her supporting figures: Iowa has not gone a full non-Covid season with fewer than eight wins since 2014, averaging 8.7 wins over the last 12 years, though she notes two of those totals include bowl wins. She expects that consistency to carry against one of the Big Ten's more manageable schedules, flagging one genuinely hard three-week early stretch — at Michigan, hosting Ohio State, then at Washington — after which she sees no obvious loss.

She expects the championship culture and style built at FCS level to translate immediately to the reshaped Mountain West, but argues the first-year schedule is unfriendly for a programme making the jump — including a non-conference meeting with an old rival in Jacksonville State, itself among the Conference USA favourites.

She gives Boise State the benefit of the doubt as the top G6 side on programme history and returning production, but was caught off guard to see them as short as 5-1 to make the playoff, and thinks the G6 slot could be wide open. Her specific pricing argument: most books have New Mexico and UNLV on the same line to win the Mountain West and on season win totals, yet UNLV is 10-1 to make the playoff and New Mexico 20-1.

They avoid Indiana altogether, whom she calls their Kryptonite last season; road trips to USC and Ohio State will be challenging and they host Michigan and Washington at Autzen, but her instinct is they lose no more than one of those. She notes Oregon has lost a combined five games in three years and calls them the model of consistency, with talent returning.

Jonathan Von Tobel|AUBURN OVER 6.5 WINS.summary: Von Tobel says to call him crazy but he is buying the South Florida takeover at Auburn. Byrum Brown amassed 4,238 combined passing and rushing yards with 42 total touchdowns last year and is, in his view, one of the best quarterbacks in the country; two of his South Florida receivers come with him. Defensive coordinator DJ Durkin remains on staff, and Von Tobel rates him among the best defensive play-callers in college football over the last three seasons. He concludes Auburn has what it needs to be a surprise SEC contender.
Jonathan Von Tobel|AUBURN OVER 6.5 WINS.depends_on: quarterback (Byrum Brown) and the receivers who transferred with him; coordinator continuity (Durkin)

Jonathan Von Tobel|NORTH DAKOTA STATE UN.summary: Von Tobel says he is not buying the seamless transition the market is selling. North Dakota State lost significant talent to the portal including two First-Team All-MVFC offensive linemen, returns just 10 starters, and brought in zero starters via the portal — only three Power Four transfers, one of them a punter from Minnesota. He contrasts that with UNLV and New Mexico at the top of the Mountain West, who retooled with transfer talent from across the country, and concludes internal promotion and development may work for the Bison long-term but not this season.

Jonathan Von Tobel|AIR FORCE OVER 7.5 WI.summary: Von Tobel calls this one of the season's coming surprises. Air Force averaged 29.8 points and 407 yards per game last season and ranked 11th nationally in EPA per play, 15th in both EPA per play rushing and rushing success rate. Liam Szarka returns at quarterback, and he expects the defense to improve under Steve Russ, a former Troy Calhoun staff member, as coordinator. He sees eight or more wins and a possible Mountain West title game berth.

Hawaii returns preseason Mountain West Offensive Player of the Year Micah Alejado, who completed 66% of his passes for 3,106 yards with 24 touchdowns against nine interceptions last season while playing on a bad ankle. With a year of starting behind him and his health back, Von Tobel expects him and the team to be excellent, and notes Hawaii hosts New Mexico, UNLV and North Dakota State.

He cites fourth-quarter form last season — 83.6% completions at 8.5 yards per attempt for nine touchdowns — and a full season now behind him. Stockton leads a title contender in the SEC, so Von Tobel expects the moments to be there along with the benefit of the doubt from voters, and reduces the case to a sentence: he is the starting quarterback for a 10-plus win SEC team.

John McKechnie|MIAMI (FL) TO WIN NATIONA.summary: McKechnie argues roster continuity is overrated in this era and that elite teams reload on the fly by managing the portal best. Miami came up just short of a national title last year and, despite notable losses in the trenches, he thinks they may be better this time. They upgraded at quarterback with Darian Mensah arriving from Duke, and his top target Cooper Barkate comes with him on a 72-catch, 1,106-yard, seven-touchdown season. Adding that pair to an offense already carrying elite line and skill talent such as Malachi Toney gives him something serious.

His view is that the defense will keep Texas A&M in games while the offense lets them down at key moments, against a schedule featuring trips to Baton Rouge, Tuscaloosa and Norman plus home games with Texas and Tennessee.
